sense: an organized body: an association, a company, an institution

terms.gloss: an association formed for a common purpose; a company
evidence: Cic. Sest. 32: nūlla Rōmae societās vectīgālium, nūllum conlēgium aut concilium
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: union for a common purpose, not a mere gathering; also a partnership, and a company of tax-farmers or traders.

terms.gloss: a body of colleagues or members: a guild, a college, a corporation
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: persons united by the same office or calling, or living by common rules.

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.157: cōnsociātiō hominum atque commūnitās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically the abstract union of people (Cicero); Morgan–Owens takes it, from twentieth-century Church Latin, for an organization.

sources: Lewis & Short: societas · Lewis & Short: collegium · Lewis & Short: consociatio · Lewis & Short: sodalitas
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: organization, society, association.
